title: Preparation and Photoacoustic Analysis of Cellular Vehicles Containing Gold Nanorods
protocol: Purify 24 ml CTAB-capped gold nanorods at a concentration of 450 µM Au by two cycles of centrifugation (12,000 x g, 30 min) and decantation.
Use 500 µM aqueous CTAB as a washing solution during purification steps.
Transfer the particles into 6 ml 100 mM acetate buffer at pH 5 containing 500 µM CTAB and 0.005% (v/v) polysorbate 20 after centrifugation.
Add 30 µl 10 mM aqueous alpha-methoxy-omega-mercapto-poly(ethylene glycol) (MW ~ 5,000) and leave to react for 30 min at 37 °C.
Add 30 µl 100 mM (11-Mercaptoundecyl)-N,N,N-trimethylammonium bromide in dimethyl sulfoxide and leave at rest for 24 hr at 37 °C.
Add 18 ml of 0.005% (v/v) polysorbate 20 in water to the particles.
Purify the particles by centrifugation at 12,000 x g for 30 min and decantation; repeat four times.
Wash the particles with 0.005% (v/v) polysorbate 20 in water during purification cycles.
Transfer the purified particles into 2.4 ml of sterile PBS at pH 7.4.
Plate 5 x 10^5 cells in four Petri dishes of 60 mm diameter and allow them to grow for 24 hours under standard culture conditions (37°C, 5% CO2).
Add an aliquot of 4.5 mM Au cationic gold nanorods in PBS to achieve a final concentration of 100 μM Au in each Petri dish.
Incubate the Petri dishes for 24 hours under standard culture conditions (37°C, 5% CO2).
Observe cells under an optical microscope to confirm their good condition and morphology.
Detach cells using a scraper from two Petri dishes.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 120 x g for 6 minutes to eliminate excess cationic gold nanorods.
Suspend the cellular pellet in 2 ml PBS.
Count the cells using a Bürker chamber.
Centrifuge a suspension containing 2 x 10^6 cells at 120 x g for 6 minutes.
Fix the cell pellet in 2 ml of 3.6% (w/v) formaldehyde in PBS for ten minutes at room temperature.
Wash the fixed cell pellet three times by centrifugation at 120 x g for 6 minutes using PBS as the washing solution.
Reconstitute low molecular weight chitosan in an acidified (pH 4.5) solution.
Thoroughly mix the chitosan solution and let it homogenize for 24 hours at 40°C.
Mix murine macrophages containing cationic gold nanorods with 500 µl of chitosan solution.
Pour 250 mg of the mixture into polystyrene molds to form ~50 µm thick phantoms.
Leave the molds under a nitrogen stream for 24 hours.
Treat the samples with 500 µl of 1 M NaOH to induce cross-linking.
Rinse the treated samples with 10 ml of ultrapure water.
Suspend a chitosan film containing macrophages in DI water using a plastic holder immersed in a Petri dish.
Maintain a distance of ~5 mm from the bottom of the plate when suspending the sample.
Place the suspended sample on a micrometric XY stage to control its position accurately.
Focus a laser beam with ~5 nsec pulse duration perpendicular to the film surface, using an optical parametric oscillator pumped by the third harmonic of a Q-switched Nd:YAG laser.
Place an attenuator in front of the laser exit to tune the laser fluence.
Use a beam splitter to focus part of the laser beam to an energy meter.
Monitor fluence fluctuations with an oscilloscope.
Maintain optical fluence below 1 mJ/cm2 per pulse during alignment.
Dip an ultrasound transducer into the Petri dish ~2 mm off the film surface.
Adjust the transducer position using micrometric translations and rotational stages.
Maximize PA signal emitted from the film by adjusting the transducer's position.
Irradiate a random point of the sample at a fluence around 1 mJ/cm2 per pulse for at least 500 pulses.
For each pulse, acquire the corresponding PA signal from the ultrasound transducer.
Acquire laser fluence from the energy meter with an oscilloscope.
Calculate the average fluence as FLOtrial.
Determine the intensity of the PA signal as its peak-to-peak amplitude.
Normalize the amplitude of each PA signal to the ratio of its own fluence to FLOtrial.
Analyze the trend of normalized PA intensity as a function of pulse number.
Verify the stability of the normalized PA intensity over time.
In the case of instability, repeat steps with a lower value of FLOtrial.
In the case of stability, repeat them with a value of FLOtrial higher by ~10% until loss of stability arises.
Set the probe fluence FLO as the second highest value of FLOtrial that ensures stability.
Choose another random point on the sample and probe an average PA intensity (ILOa) over 500 pulses at FLO.
Set a nominal fluence greater than FLO and deliver 50 pulses, naming their average fluence as Fexc.
Probe an average PA intensity (ILOb) over 500 pulses at FLO once again.
Calculate the ratio R = ILOb / ILOa.
Use the micrometric XY stage to move the film and change the sample point randomly.
Repeat steps with different values of Fexc, taking a few values of R below, around, and above unity (15 points are reasonable).
Plot R as a function of Fexc and identify reshaping threshold fluence Fth when R begins to differ from one beyond statistical uncertainty.
